ledger.what_new: New debate over runway buffer requirement; crushable-concrete tech (EMAS) credited with saving ~500 lives
ledger.unique: Introduces EMAS runway-arrestor technology and policy debate angle

clusters.state_of_play: An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 cargo plane (Flight 7598) arriving from Puerto Rico overran a diagonal runway at Miami International Airport shortly before 2 p.m. EDT Sunday, struck two vehicles — a cleaning-company van and an SUV — and caught fire, killing at least 5 people and injuring five others (three critically); the two-person crew survived. NTSB recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders and is examining whether the plane touched down too far down the runway to stop safely; the aircraft came to rest about 1,300 feet past the runway end. All runways closed; FAA and NTSB continue investigating.
